title: Early music, cornet in the church boys band under Professor Young
summary: Scott recalls childhood attraction to music, the church boys band, being put on cornet at nine, and his 1903 birth date.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I don't know where I got my musical talent. Neither one of my parents was musically inclined or knew anything about music. But ever since I was a very small child, music always appealed to me. And I was told by my parents that when I was very, very small, whenever any music or big band passed or something, they couldn't control me, they couldn't hold me. I had to go, wanted to go where they were. I wanted to be with them.

It went on like that, my mother and father were very religious people. And they used to go to church every Sunday. So my father finally told my mother, said, maybe he's got something in him that's musically inclined. He said, I just heard that down at the church they're having a boys band they're forming, a children's band, and maybe he could get into that.

Mama said, well, take him down then and see. Well, I had got a pair of little wooden sticks, and I used to practice with the -- drumming all over everything, used to get a spanking every time I made a little noise. And I went down with my father and had my little wooden sticks with me. It was a boys band, but everybody in there wanted to be a drummer, said Professor Young. So we had too many drummers. They put me on a cornet. They needed cornets, they (unintelligible). Well, that was music.
When were you-- what was the --
I was nine years old at the time.
What is your correct date of birth?
1903? And the month and the day?
So you were nine when they gave you a coronet.
So you were nine when they gave you the coronet.

Oh, that was music. And he was very good, that Professor Young. He taught basic music. And I was eager to learn, and he said I was a good pupil. And I learned how to play coronet from him. Well, I went very religiously and regularly to the rehearsals, and I learned to play. And I used to practice at home. They let me play until they got tired and told me to stop that noise, and I had to stop.
